translationRepairs: A visitor called Master Guo practiced divination west of the river, and Guo Pu apprenticed himself to him.
A visitor called Master Guo practiced divination in Hedong, and Guo Pu apprenticed himself to him.
河東 is the commandery Hedong, east of the Yellow River; “west of the river” reverses the geography. The replacement names the place correctly without adding unstated matter.
There was a Master Guo who lodged west of the river and mastered divination; Pu studied under him.
There was a Master Guo who lodged in Hedong and mastered divination; Pu studied under him.
客居河東 means Master Guo sojourned in Hedong; the literal “west of the river” is the same geographic error. “Lodged in Hedong” matches both 客居 and the place name.
Pu's disciple Zhao Zai once stole The Satchel of Azure Fragrance; before he could read it fire burned it.
Pu's disciple Zhao Zai once stole the Azure Satchel text; before he could read it fire burned it.
《青襄書》 is the same Qingnang satchel text as 《青囊中書》 in the preceding sentence; 襄 is a graphic variant of 囊, not “fragrance.”
He reached General Zhao Gu—happened Guo's ridden fine horse died—Guo prized it—did not receive guests.
He reached General Zhao Gu—it happened that Gu's ridden fine horse died—Gu prized it—did not receive guests.
會固所乘良馬死，固惜之 names Zhao Gu (固) as owner and mourner; the original English wrongly assigns both acts to Guo Pu.
Guo hurried out—said: Sir can revive my horse?
Gu hurried out—said: Sir can revive my horse?
固趨出 is Zhao Gu hurrying out to question Guo Pu; rendering the subject as Guo reverses speaker and addressee.
Guo acted as said—indeed obtained one thing resembling monkey—carried back.
Gu acted as said—indeed obtained one thing resembling a monkey—carried it back.
固如其言 makes Zhao Gu the agent who follows Guo Pu’s instructions; “Guo acted as said” misattributes the retrieval.
Guo marvelled at him—greatly added provisions.
Gu marvelled at him—greatly added provisions.
固奇之，厚加資給 is Zhao Gu marvelling at Guo Pu and supplying him; the original makes Guo the giver.

While Yuan Emperor still held Ye Wang Dao had Guo Pu cast lots; the hexagram ran Concord turning into Well: "A county northeast bearing the syllable Wu will yield bronze clappers proving Heaven's mandate.

While Yuan Emperor still held Ye, Wang Dao had Guo Pu cast lots; the hexagram ran Concord turning into Well: "A county northeast bearing the syllable Wu will yield bronze clappers proving Heaven's mandate.
元帝初鎮鄴 and 導令璞筮之 are successive clauses; without a boundary after Ye the English fuses the garrison place with Wang Dao’s name. The comma restores the two agents.
This matches Xi Ci's line that ancient kings shaped music to magnify virtue and offered it lavishly on high."
This matches the hexagram statement that former kings made music to honor virtue and offered it richly to the Supreme Lord."
繇辭 is the hexagram’s oracular wording, not the Xici (繫辭). The quoted 先王以作樂崇德，殷薦之上帝 is that statement, and 上帝 is the Supreme Lord, not a vague “on high.”
Xi commentary so-called 'Former kings used making music honour virtue—richly present Supreme Lord' those.
Hexagram statement so-called 'Former kings used making music honour virtue—richly present Supreme Lord' those.
“Xi commentary” misnames 繇辭 as the Xici. The proposed “Line text” still suggests 爻辭 rather than the hexagram’s oracular statement, so the literal field should read “Hexagram statement.”
His Southern Suburb Fu delighted the throne and earned appointment as assistant editor.
Later he again composed the Southern Suburb Fu; the emperor saw and praised it and appointed him Assistant in the Imperial Library.

後復作 and 帝見而嘉之 are omitted in the original, and 著作佐郎 is not a generic “assistant editor.” The proposal restates 嘉之 as both “delighted” and “saw and praised.” The revised sentence keeps the later composition, the emperor’s seeing and praising, and the named office.
While Ming Emperor was heir Wen Qiao and Yu Liang enjoyed rustic friendship with him; Guo Pu matched them in scholarship and critics admired the pairing.

While the Ming Emperor was in the Eastern Palace, he enjoyed a commoner's friendship with Wen Qiao and Yu Liang; Guo Pu was also esteemed for talent and learning, ranked equal to Qiao and Liang, and critics praised him.
明帝之在東宮，與溫嶠、庾亮並有布衣之好 assigns the commoner’s friendship to the heir with Wen Qiao and Yu Liang; 璞亦以才學見重 is a separate comparison. The original fuses “heir” with Wen Qiao and reverses those relations.

As for Zhuang Zhou lounging in Qiyuan, Lao Lai wandering in forest caves, Yan Ping settling into clarity in the dusty market, Mei Zhen hiding among market servants, Master Liang chanting and whistling while correcting his traces, Jiao Xian in muddled stump-like stillness, Ruan Gong drunk and selling pride, and old Zhai vanishing in an instant:

As for Zhuang Zhou lounging in Qiyuan, Lao Lai wandering in forest caves, Yan Ping settling into clarity in the dusty market, Mei Zhen hiding among market servants, Master Liang chanting and whistling while lifting his traces, Jiao Xian in muddled stump-like stillness, Ruan Gong drunk and selling pride, and old Zhai vanishing in an instant:

矯跡 in this recluse catalogue means raising or withdrawing one’s footsteps from the world, not morally “correcting” traces. “Lifting his traces” restores that sense and keeps the line’s parallel diction.
If I should unfortunately prove wrong, it will still leave Your Majesty with the worry of sitting uneasily.
If I should unfortunately prove correct, it will certainly leave Your Majesty with the worry of sitting uneasily.
不幸謬中 is the humble “if I should unluckily hit the mark”; 中 is a successful hit, not being wrong, and 必 is “certainly,” not “still.”
He answered: "It can bring the Son of Heaven to ask, that is all."
The host answered: "It can bring the Son of Heaven to ask, that is all."
After 帝曰 the reply 答曰 continues the burial host of 主人曰, not the emperor. Naming “the host” prevents that misattribution.
They withdrew whispering: "His silence feared frank speech—or heaven seized Wang Dun's wits.
They withdrew whispering: "Pu's indecisive answer meant he dared not speak—or heaven seized Wang Dun's wits.
璞對不了，是不敢有言 explains the indecisive hexagram answer as a refusal to speak, not “silence feared frank speech.” The replacement matches that gloss.
Walking out Guo Pu asked where they headed.
Walking out Guo Pu asked the executioner where they were headed.
謂行刑者欲何之 addresses the executioner; the original omits that addressee.
Bing struck his breast and sighed in regret.
撫心歎恨 is the idiom of striking the breast in remorse, not a word-for-word “stroked heart.” The replacement is grammatical and faithful.
Yu Bing's son Yu Yun governed Guangzhou where a concubine secretly raised a newborn white pup.

Later Yu Bing's son Yu Yun was inspector of Guangzhou. Inside a concubine's chamber there suddenly appeared a newborn white puppy; no one knew where it came from. The concubine secretly cherished it and did not let Yun know.
The original drops 忽有, 莫知所由來, and 不令蘊知. Those details—the pup’s sudden unknown origin and the concubine hiding it from Yun—are required by the omen. The replacement restores them.
During Taian Ge Hong joined Gu Mi's loyal army against Shi Bing as commandant, routed a column, and earned promotion to Wave-Pacifying general.

During Taian, Shi Bing rebelled. Gu Mi, grand administrator of Wuxing, became commander of a loyalist army and with Zhou Qi and others raised troops against him. Gu Mi's proclamation made Ge Hong commandant of troops; Hong attacked Shi Bing's detached force, defeated it, and was promoted to General Who Calms the Waves.
太安中，石冰作亂 is Shi Bing’s rebellion; 吳興太守顧秘 and 與周玘等 are omitted, and 將兵都尉 / 伏波將軍 are compressed. The replacement restores the sequence and named offices.
Early in Xianhe Wang Dao named him prefect clerk, then chancellor aide, then consultant.
Early in Xianhe, Wang Dao summoned him to fill the post of prefectural chief clerk; he was transferred as aide to the Minister of Education and promoted to consultant adviser.
咸和初，司徒導 is the era then Wang Dao as Minister of Education, not a fused “Xianhe Wang Dao.” 司徒掾 is an aide to the situ, not a chancellor’s aide, and 諮議參軍 is consultant adviser.
Deng Yue petitioned him as governor of Eastern Office yet again he declined.
Deng Yue petitioned to have him fill the post of grand administrator of Dongguan, but he again declined.
東官太守 is grand administrator of Dongguan commandery; 官 is the place name, not “office.”
Painting Mother Mo and expecting Yangzhou beauties to praise it—
Adorning Mother Mo's utter ugliness and seeking a matchmaker's flattering praise—
求媒陽之美談 is seeking a matchmaker’s praise of adorned Mother Mo; 媒陽 is not Yangzhou. The original invents a place.
Yao Li lifting tripods broke Qin men's sinews—
Frail Yao Li forcing himself into a cauldron-lifting feat is why Qin men tore their sinews—

要離之羸而強赴扛鼎之勢 contrasts Yao Li’s frailty with forced cauldron-lifting; he did not lift tripods and thereby break Qin sinews. The proposal has the right contrast but “frailty forced into” is ungrammatical.
Confucians mock immortal scriptures—some even slander the true teaching.
Worldly Confucians only cling to the Duke of Zhou and Confucius and distrust immortal books—they not only laugh them off as grandiose but will slander what is true.

世儒徒知服膺周孔，莫信神仙之書 names worldly Ruists who only embrace the Duke of Zhou and Confucius and distrust immortal books, then 不但大而笑之，又將謗毀真正. Compressing this to “Confucians mock” drops 周孔 and the two-stage scorn.
